terms.term: A Dart file under lib/ but outside lib/src/ that is a library rather than a part. Other packages may import it, so its export namespace is the package's public API.
Everything a library makes visible to its importers: its own public declarations plus everything it re-exports with export directives, after show and hide combinators are applied.

A file build_runner tracks. Builders can only read build sources through the build step, and a build step reruns only when one of the sources it read changes. The default sources are lib/, bin/, test/, example/, tool/, web/, pubspec.yaml, pubspec.lock, README, CHANGELOG and LICENSE.
The directory .dart_tool/build/generated where build_runner keeps the outputs of builders with build_to: cache.
The location of an output that a builder with build_to: source writes into the package itself, next to your sources. The committed API dump is such an output.
dart run build_runner build --only-check: builds everything, writes nothing, and fails when an output in the package path differs from the file on disk. Available since build_runner 2.16.0.
The per-file line execution counts the Dart VM reports for a test run. package:coverage merges and formats them.
A plain-text coverage format (lcov.info) that IDEs, Codecov, Coveralls, SonarQube and genhtml read.
Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures: the public identifier of a known vulnerability, such as CVE-2020-35669.
A GitHub Security Advisory identifier, such as GHSA-4rgh-jx4f-qfcq. Advisories for pub packages are the data source Trivy uses for Dart.
The standard short name of a license, such as MIT, BSD-3-Clause or GPL-3.0.
Trivy's classification of a license by obligation: forbidden, restricted, reciprocal, notice, permissive or unencumbered. Each category maps to a severity.

A package reachable from the dependencies section of the root pubspec.yaml - code that consumers of your package or users of your app actually receive. Packages reachable only through dev_dependencies are not shipped.
A monorepo of Dart packages resolved together, with one pubspec.lock and one .dart_tool directory in the workspace root.
The vulnerability database Trivy downloads from mirror.gcr.io/aquasec/trivy-db and caches, by default in ~/.cache/trivy. Only the vulnerability scans need it.
A Trivy secret scanning rule that suppresses findings, for example in paths that commonly hold test fixtures.
A temporary directory Inspectra copies the selected files into before it runs Trivy, so that Trivy sees exactly those files under their package-relative paths. It is deleted when the scan ends.
The analysis_options.yaml file in the package root: which lint rules run, which files the analyzer excludes, how severe each diagnostic is, and the formatter's page width.
A finding of the Dart analyzer: a compile-time error, a warning, a hint or a lint, each with a severity of error, warning or info.
